name: Challah — Dough Tithe (Laws of Hallah)
notes: Detailed laws of the challah obligation: minimum measure (five-fourths of a kav), who is obligated, when the obligation begins (rolling/formation of crust), and how it is separated

name: Minimum Measure for Challah (Shiur Challah)
notes: The minimum amount of dough (five-fourths of a kav) that triggers the challah obligation, and the proportion to be separated (1/24 for private bakers, 1/48 for commercial bakers)

name: Challah Outside the Land of Israel
notes: Differences in challah law between the Land of Israel, Syria, and lands further outside; three territorial zones with different obligations; two challah portions in Syria

name: Challah Obligation for Gentile Dough
notes: Whether dough belonging to or made by a non-Jew is subject to challah; cases of conversion and partnership with a non-Jew

name: Combining Different Grain Species for Challah
notes: Rules about which of the five grain species combine with each other to reach the minimum measure for challah; wheat and spelt combine, barley with other species except wheat, etc.

name: Challah and Ritual Purity
notes: Separating challah in a state of cleanness vs. uncleanness; proportions for intentionally vs. unintentionally defiled dough; separating from clean dough to exempt unclean dough

name: Challah and Hekdesh (Dedicated Dough)
notes: Effect of dedicating dough to the Temple before or after reaching the point of obligation on challah liability; parallel with tithes and produce dedicated before ripening

name: Dough Mixed with Rice or Non-Grain Ingredients
notes: Whether dough containing rice or other non-obligated species mixed with grain is subject to challah; depends on whether it has the taste of grain

name: Commercial Baker's Challah
notes: Commercial bakers separate a smaller proportion (1/48) than private individuals (1/24); women selling in the market treated like commercial bakers

name: Challah from Demai Dough
notes: Separating challah from demai (doubtfully tithed produce); challah for demai can be taken from clean dough for unclean, and even from dough not in close proximity

name: Three Territories for Challah (Land of Israel, Syria, Abroad)
notes: Rabban Gamliel's division of three zones — from Israel to Chezib (one challah portion), from Chezib to the river (two portions), and beyond the river (two portions with different rules for priest)

name: Point at Which Dough Becomes Obligated in Challah
notes: The rolling/kneading (galgul) for wheat or formation of solid mass for barley as the trigger for the challah obligation; eating before this point vs. liability for death afterwards

name: Geographic Restrictions on Bikkurim and Priestly Gifts
hebrew: גבולות ארץ ישראל לבכורים ומתנות כהונה
notes: Whether bikkurim, firstlings, and other priestly gifts brought from Syria, Babylon, or Alexandria are accepted; the rule that purchasing land in Syria is like purchasing land in the outskirts of Jerusalem

name: Distribution of Priestly Gifts to Any Priest
notes: List of items that may be given to any priest (devoted things, firstlings, pidyon haben, shoulder/cheeks/maw, first fleece, bikkurim, etc.) vs. items requiring specific conditions

name: Challah Parallels to Terumah
notes: Rules shared between challah and terumah: karet for intentional consumption by non-priest, added fifth for inadvertent consumption, nullification in 101 parts, require handwashing and sunset, cannot separate from pure for impure

name: Israelite Tenant Farmer in Syria
notes: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabban Gamliel whether an Israelite who rents land from a non-Jew in Syria is liable for tithes and shemitah; eventual ruling followed Rabban Gamliel in both

name: Challah Obligation on Todah Loaves and Nazirite Wafers
notes: Todah loaves and nazirite wafers made for personal use are exempt from challah; if made for sale they are subject to challah
